entries.topic: UN layer: the founding of the UN, UNSCOP, all 57 votes on Resolution 181, the reported pressure campaign, the 1948 recognitions and the 1949 admission (Nov 2026)
claims: Charter signed at San Francisco on 26 June 1945 by 50 countries; the UN came into existence on 24 Oct 1945. It replaced the League of Nations, which had effectively closed in 1939.
May 1947: the UN formed the Special Committee on Palestine (UNSCOP).

3 Sept 1947: UNSCOP's majority (Canada, Czechoslovakia, Guatemala, the Netherlands, Peru, Sweden, Uruguay) proposed partition with economic union; India, Iran and Yugoslavia proposed a federal state; Australia abstained.
Canada sat on UNSCOP and backed its majority plan for partition.
Czechoslovakia sat on UNSCOP and backed its majority plan for partition.
Guatemala sat on UNSCOP and backed its majority plan for partition.
Netherlands sat on UNSCOP and backed its majority plan for partition.
Peru sat on UNSCOP and backed its majority plan for partition.
Sweden sat on UNSCOP and backed its majority plan for partition.
Uruguay sat on UNSCOP and backed its majority plan for partition.
India sat on UNSCOP and backed the minority plan for a federal state.
Iran sat on UNSCOP and backed the minority plan for a federal state.
Yugoslavia sat on UNSCOP and backed the minority plan for a federal state.

29 Nov 1947: adopted 33 to 13 with 10 abstentions and 1 absent. It needed two-thirds of the votes cast, abstentions not counted, among the 57 members; held on the original date it would have had a majority but not two-thirds.
Byelorussian SSR voted for partition, 29 Nov 1947.
Costa Rica voted for partition, 29 Nov 1947.
Dominican Republic voted for partition, 29 Nov 1947.
New Zealand voted for partition, 29 Nov 1947.
Ukrainian SSR voted for partition, 29 Nov 1947.
Union of South Africa voted for partition, 29 Nov 1947.
United States voted for partition, 29 Nov 1947.
Soviet Union voted for partition, 29 Nov 1947.
Saudi Arabia voted against partition, 29 Nov 1947.
El Salvador abstained on partition, 29 Nov 1947.
United Kingdom abstained on partition, 29 Nov 1947.
Siam was absent: its credentials were cancelled after it voted against partition in committee on 25 Nov 1947.
The Philippine delegate had argued against partition; "after a phone call from Washington, the representative was recalled and the Philippines' vote changed."
"The promise of a five million dollar loan may or may not have secured Haiti's vote for partition."
Harvey S. Firestone Jr., with major holdings in Liberia, pressured the Liberian government; Liberia's ambassador complained the US delegation threatened aid cuts.
Bernard Baruch visited France's delegate and implied that a French vote against might block planned American aid to France.
A telegram signed by 26 senators with influence over foreign-aid bills was sent to wavering countries.
Under Secretary Robert Lovett reported that "bribes and threats were being used, even of American sanctions against Liberia and Nicaragua."
Sam Zemurray reportedly pressured Central American states.
The vote was postponed by three days after filibustering by the Zionist delegation; supporters used the delay to press states not yet backing the resolution.
Nehru said "the Zionists had tried to bribe India with millions"; Ambassador Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit reportedly received threats unless she "voted right".
The Arab states warned that endorsing partition might bring an oil embargo or a realignment with the Soviet bloc.
14 May 1948: the Declaration cited Resolution 181 among its legal bases.
All 37 members of the Provisional State Council were to sign; 25 signed at the Tel Aviv Museum on 14 May 1948, with spaces left for the 12 absent.
14 May 1948: recognized Israel, de facto (de jure 31 Jan 1949).
17 May 1948: recognized Israel, de jure, the first state to grant it.
18 May 1948: recognized Israel, de facto and de jure.
19 May 1948: recognized Israel, de facto, the first in Latin America.
11 Sept 1948: recognized Israel, de facto; formal on 8 Nov 1948.
4 Mar 1949: Security Council Resolution 69 recommended admission.
11 May 1949: Israel admitted to the UN, 37 to 12 with 9 abstentions; the resolution recalls Resolutions 181 (Jerusalem) and 194 (refugees) and notes Israel's declarations on implementing them.
